description.narrative: The objective of the AF is to improve inclusiveness of school funding management and enhance support to teachersa?? professional development while increasing transition rates of poor and at-risk students.

The objective of the Decentralizing Funding to Schools Project is to help improve and expand Myanmar's School Grants Program and Student Stipends Program. There are three components to the project, the first component being expansion and improvement of the school grants program. All schools with primary students currently supported by government budget funding are eligible for participation in the school grants program. Expansion of the program, therefore, will mean increasing the size of annual operating grants to schools from approximately US$250, US$400 and US$500 per school for small, medium and large schools, respectively, to targets of US$900, US$1,200 and US$1,800 per school, respectively, over a four year period. The second component is the expansion and improvement of the student stipends program. While all government-supported schools in Myanmar are nominally eligible to participate in the existing student stipends program, the small size of the program (11,000 stipends to be awarded nationwide) effectively means that, while most schools apply for stipends funding, few schools are actually selected to participate in the program and those that do participate would have, in most cases, no more than two stipend students. Finally, the third component is the capacity improvement to strengthen monitoring and implementation of programs. This project will focus on training, and on conducting a baseline assessment of early grade reading. On training, Ministry of Education, or MoE will design and begin implementing a national training program during school year 2014-15 aimed at introducing the new school grants and stipends program to township officials and school headmasters.

title.narrative: 4. Townships having transferred funds to at least 80 percent of their schools, in accordance with latest SISP guidelines (DLIs 5, 8, 11, 17, and 21)

comment.narrative:
<p>DFSP original target 200 townships was overachieved at 115.5% as DLI (11) was verified by third party monitoring as 231 townships (Cardno Y1 report dated 30 April 2018).</p>
<p>For the Additional Financing Revised target 280 townships, it was 100% achieved verified by third party monitoring as 330 townships transferred funds to 99.1 % of their schools in accordance with SISP guidelines. (Cardno Y6 Report, DLI 17) </p>

<p>DFSP original target was fully achieved. The guidelines for School Improvement Support program (SISP) and Student Stipends program (SSP) were developed and endorsed by MoE in 2014-2015 SY. Based on the lessons learned from project year one implementation, the guidelines were revised in 2015-2016 and 2016-2017 respectively. </p>

<p>For the Additional Financing, both SISP and SSP guidelines were revised again in 2018-2019 SY to include social inclusion, community consultations, complaint mechanism, and BMY specific approach in the SISP and SSP.</p>

<p>The operational guideline for AF new component, 'Teacher Mentoring and School Cluster Support program', and 'Mentoring Handbook' were developed and endorsed by MoE in 2017-2018 SYand refined in 2018-2019 SY.</p>

<p>The teachers' guide for Early Grade Reading Intervention Pilot (EGRI) was developed in 2018-2019 SY. The operational guideline was developed in 2019-2020. </p>

<p>This indicator was fully achieved.</p>
<p>This indicator was overachieved at 101.7 %. The detailed beneficiary breakdown is attached in the Annex 7 Supporting Documents.</p>

comment.narrative:

title.narrative: 23. System for learning assessment at the primary level

comment.narrative: <p>With the Bank's technical assistance, MOE has carried out regular rounds of EGRA and EGMA since 2013-2014 SY, including regional representative assessment as well as nationally representative assessment. With support from Unicef, MOE recently joined the the SEA-PLM assessment. Further steps in strengthening national assessment are underway with support from DFID. </p>

<p>This indicator was fully achieved. The Student Stipends program operational guideline was first developed when the project came into effective in 2014 and revised two times during later years based on the process monitoring findings. </p>

title.narrative: 11. School heads trained in implementing programs, in accordance with the latest guidelines (non-cumulative)

comment.narrative:
<p>DFSP original target was 160% overachieved as 48,010 SHs trained (MoE Status report 2017-2018) because school grants program was expanded to all Middle and High schools, and Monastic schools in country. After year one implementation, MoE decided to expand the school grants provision to middle, high and monastic schools, not just limited to primary level.</p>
<p>For AF target, it was 99% achieved (MoE Status report 2019-2020 SY).</p>

title.narrative: 8. Large schools which have opened and use a bank account to receive their school grants

comment.narrative: <p>Large schools were identified as having more than 401 students attending. During implementation period, it was found out that the primary schools head position was not entitled for drawing rights to open school bank accounts in Myanma Economic Banks (MEBs) according to government financial rules and regulations. Government funds like school grants were also not allowed to bedeposited in local private banks. High schools and large middle schools in urban areas were able to open school bank accounts at the MEBs. The remote schools could not open bank accounts due to remoteness and high transport charges. The MoE admin data was not complete as it showed data from eight States and Regions, no data available for the rest 10 States and Regions. Out of 5,155 largeschools, 1,123 schools opened bank accounts. The percentage was  21.8 %. This target was overly ambitious and not reflecting the context of the government financial rules and regulations.</p>

title.narrative: 9. Students having received stipends payment in accordance with the latest SSP guidelines (DLIs 4, 7, 10, 17, and 21)

comment.narrative:
<p>DFSP original target of stipend payment to 100,000 students in 2018 was overachieved at 151,175 (151%). This indicator was verified by third party monitoring (DLI Verification report, May 2019). </p>
<p>AF revised target of 250,000 students was overachieved as 305,503 students in 2019-2020 at 122% based on MoE admin data. The number of stipend students was based on 2019-20 school year total (244,331) and added with the number of Grade 11 stipend students (61,172) who left the basic education system after Grade 11in 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018 and 2018-2019 school years. The number were 2,130, 7,322, 14,305, 18,811, and 18,604 respectively.</p>

title.narrative: 14. Reports analyzing impacts of supported programs are available (DLI18 and 22)

comment.narrative: <p>(DLI 18) A report on 4 rounds of EGRA and one round of EGMA was completed in January 2021. A draft report on the impact of a small early grade reading intervention pilot was completed in April 2021. MOE also implemented another round of national level of EGRA and EGMA in January and February 2020. Data entry was completed for EGRA but EGMA data entry remained unfinished when military coup occurred in February 2021. The sample includes 266 schools and approximately 10,000 Grade 1 and Grade 3 students</p>

title.narrative: 1. Schools which spend improvement funding after (new) inclusive consultations with parents and community (DLI13)

comment.narrative: <p>As status of 2019-2020 school year, 24.9 % of schools spent school funding after inclusive consultation with parents and communities. The achievement was verified by the third party monitoring. Due to the weak internal reporting mechanism within the MoE subordinate levels, the school reports were not collected in a timely manner. To address this issue, MoE conducted Refresher trainingon social inclusion and GRM to all (47,448) school heads (SHs) using ODK application for direct reporting. The cascade training started in October 2019 and completed in January 2020. Right after the training, SHs started to submit their reports through ODK App till mid-March when the COVID pandemic hit Myanmar and all schools closed. A total of 9,200 schools submitted and 8,786 reported that social assessment (SA) and community consultations were completed. It was 96% achievement but cannot be verified because of COVID lockdowns and school closure.</p>

title.narrative: 17. School clusters having carried out meetings in accordance with the TMCSP (DLI15 and 23)

comment.narrative:
<p>The Teacher Mentoring and School Cluster Support program has been implemented in 150 townships. It was not yet scaled up to330 townships as the project missed the last year of its implementation due to COVID pandemic. For the 2019-2020 SY, school cluster activities were carried out in 2,974 clusters in implementing 150 townships (MoE Status Report 2019-2020). Therefore, 2,974 clusters in 150 townships was 100% achieved, but it was 59% against the end target (5,000) for 330 townships.  </p>
<p> </p>

Therefore, the total number of mentees reached by the project was shortfall against the end target (79,000) which was expected to achieve in 330 townships. The indicator was 40.7% achieved. </p>

title.narrative: 3. Primary schools having participated in mentoring activities (DLI 23)

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator was expected to be achieved by July 2021 with full coverage of 330 implementing townships. But the project missed the final year implementation (2020-2021 School year) due to COVID school closure and was not able to scale up to new 180 townships The schools were not limited to primary level only because mentoring program included primary teachers (mentees) in middle and high schools. According to MoE Admin data reporting at the Technical Working Group (TWG) in August 2019, the participating schools in implementing 150 townships was 20,332. This number represented 43% against 47,445 total schools in 330 townships. If the percentage was calculated against the total number of schools (26,326) in implementing 150 townships, it was 77 %. This indicator was overachieved in currently implementing 150 townships, but a bit shortfall to achieve the end target because of the missing year for implementation. </p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: 16. Mentor teachers engaged, trained, and deployed in accordance with the TMCSP (DLI19)

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was fully achieved for the implementing 150 townships. 600 Mentors were recruited, trained and deployed in 150 ongoing townships. The last year of the project (2020-2021 SY) was not able to implement due to COVID school closure. Therefore, another 720 Mentors for new 180 townships were not recruited, trained, and deployed. Against the end target, this indicator was not achieved. For the school year 2019-2020, there was a delay in recruitment of 360 Mentors for 90 townships. During the COVID travel restrictions, DERPT organized on-line Refresher training for core trainers of Teacher mentoring, training modules revised into two channels: Online and in-person. The training department got ready to train newly recruited Mentors. </p>

title.narrative: 2. Average transition rate from primary to middle school of stipends recipients is higher than for comparable non-recipients

comment.narrative: <p>The baseline 5% was calculated from the World Bank Household survey 2018. The actual achievement was calculated using the data from the Stipend Student Payment Management System (SSPMS) software and the student data from the MoE C4M dataset. The comparison wasbased on the Grade 5 students in 2018-2019 school year and Grade 6 students in 2019-2020 school year. The transition rate for non-stipend students in (55) stipends program townships was 93%. The stipends students' transition rate was 102%. So, it was calculated stipend student transition rate was 9% higher than the non-stipends student rate in the same 55 townships.</p>
